categories.main_business_segments: Best Buy operates through two primary segments: Domestic (U.S. operations, including Best Buy Health) and International (Canada). The Domestic segment encompasses all U.S. states and territories and includes brands such as Best Buy, Geek Squad, Best Buy Health, and others. The International segment covers Canadian operations under the Best Buy, Best Buy Express, Best Buy Mobile, and Geek Squad brands.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Best Buy leverages an omnichannel retail platform integrating online, in-store, and in-home experiences, supported by centralized procurement, supply chain, and technology infrastructure. The company utilizes advanced inventory management, ship-from-store capabilities, and digital tools, and develops exclusive brands through global sourcing and contract manufacturing. Technology investments focus on AI-driven personalization, e-commerce, and operational efficiency.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Best Buy serves individual consumers, small businesses, and health sector clients, focusing on technology products and solutions for everyday needs. Key markets include consumer electronics, computing, appliances, entertainment, and health technology, with a growing emphasis on services such as installation, repair, and technical support. The company also targets commercial and government customers through Best Buy Business.
categories.geographic_coverage: Best Buy's operations are primarily in the United States and Canada, with 957 stores in the U.S. and 160 in Canada as of fiscal 2025. The company also supports online sales and in-home services across both countries, with a small portion of sourcing and product development activities in other regions. The U.S. accounts for the majority of revenue, with Canada representing about 8%.
categories.supply_chain_position: Best Buy operates as a downstream retailer, selling finished goods and services directly to end customers. The company sources products from manufacturers and vendors, manages distribution through its own and third-party logistics, and offers value-added services such as delivery, installation, and after-sales support. It also develops and contracts manufacturing for exclusive brands.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include enhancing omnichannel experiences, investing in AI-driven digital personalization, expanding the Best Buy Marketplace and retail media (Best Buy Ads), and driving operational efficiency. R&D efforts focus on technology integration, exclusive brand development, and health technology solutions. The company is also committed to sustainability, circular economy initiatives, and responsible sourcing.
categories.revenue_model: Best Buy generates revenue primarily through the sale of consumer electronics, appliances, and related products, both in-store and online. Additional revenue streams include services (installation, repair, memberships), commissions from third-party warranties and mobile activations, profit-sharing from branded credit cards, advertising (Best Buy Ads), and, starting in fiscal 2026, marketplace commissions.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Best Buy competes with multi-channel and online retailers (e.g., Amazon, Walmart), technology service providers, traditional store-based retailers, and vendors selling direct to consumers. The company differentiates itself through its integrated omnichannel platform, tech expertise, service offerings, and curated product assortment, but faces intense price competition and margin pressure.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In fiscal 2025, Best Buy reported $41.5 billion in revenue, a 4.4% decline from the prior year, with net earnings of $927 million. The company has experienced revenue contraction over the past three years due to industry headwinds and softer consumer demand, but maintains strong cash flow, investment-grade credit ratings, and ongoing share repurchases and dividends.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Best Buy emphasizes enriching lives through technology by combining tech expertise with personalized, human-centric service across digital, in-store, and in-home channels. Its value proposition includes a broad and curated product assortment, strong vendor partnerships, exclusive brands, comprehensive service offerings (Geek Squad, memberships), and a seamless omnichannel experience.
